items.followUp: Name two thermometric properties and state how each changes with temperature.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of a thermometer.
rubric.description: Defines a thermometer as an instrument for measuring temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it measures temperature.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of properties that vary with temperature.
rubric.description: Names thermometric properties, such as volume, pressure, electrical resistance, length, or thermoelectric emf.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one valid thermometric property.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
Basic thermometric properties include the volume of a liquid, the pressure of a gas at constant volume, and the electrical resistance of a wire.

items.followUp: Define the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire.

rubric.why: Checks identification of where the magnetic field exists.
rubric.description: States that the field is the region or space around a magnet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the region around the magnet.

rubric.why: Checks the defining effect of a magnetic field.
rubric.description: States that magnetic force can be experienced or detected there.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the magnetic force in that region.

modelAnswer: The magnetic field of a magnet is the region around it in which its magnetic force can be experienced.

items.followUp: Give one use each of a permanent magnet and an electromagnet.

rubric.why: Checks an application of permanent magnets.
rubric.description: Names a valid use of a permanent magnet, such as in a compass or loudspeaker.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid permanent-magnet application.

rubric.description: Names a valid use of an electromagnet, such as an electric bell, relay, or crane for lifting scrap iron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid electromagnet application.

modelAnswer: Permanent magnets are used in compasses and loudspeakers.
Electromagnets are used in electric bells and cranes for lifting scrap iron.

items.followUp: Describe how a magnet can be demagnetized by heating.

rubric.why: Checks identification of a valid demagnetization method.
rubric.description: Names a valid method, such as heating, hammering, or using an alternating-current solenoid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming one valid method.

rubric.why: Checks the essential procedure when using an AC solenoid or heating.
rubric.description: For the AC method, places the magnet in a solenoid carrying alternating current and slowly withdraws it; alternatively, states that the magnet is heated strongly or hammered repeatedly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid method described with its essential action.

modelAnswer: Place the magnet inside a solenoid connected to an alternating-current supply.
Slowly withdraw the magnet from the solenoid while the current is flowing.

items.followUp: Write the main steps of the scientific method and explain why experiments are performed.

rubric.why: Checks the starting stage of scientific investigation.
rubric.description: Includes observation or identification of a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for observation or identifying a problem.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the remaining scientific-method stages.
rubric.description: Includes stages such as forming a hypothesis, making deductions, experimentation, and obtaining results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least two relevant further stages.

modelAnswer: Observe a phenomenon and identify the problem.
Form a hypothesis and make deductions from it.
Test the deductions by experimentation.
Record and analyse the results; draw a conclusion.

items.followUp: State one difference between a scientific hypothesis and a theory.

rubric.why: Checks what a physical law states.
rubric.description: Explains that a law describes a consistent relationship or what happens in nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the descriptive role of a law.

rubric.why: Checks the explanatory role of a theory.
rubric.description: Explains that a theory explains why or how natural phenomena occur.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the explanatory role of a theory.

modelAnswer: A law of Physics describes a regular relationship or states what happens in nature.
A theory of Physics explains why or how the observed phenomena occur.

items.followUp: A force acts on a 3 kg body and changes its velocity from 2 m/s to 6 m/s in 4 s. Find the change in momentum and the force.

rubric.why: Checks the definition and expression for momentum.
rubric.description: Defines momentum as the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating momentum equals mass times velocity.

rubric.why: Checks Newton's second law in momentum terms.
rubric.description: States that force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum and acts in the direction of that change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the rate-of-change statement.

rubric.why: Checks the direction or proportionality part of the law.
rubric.description: States that the change in momentum is in the direction of the applied force, or that force is directly proportional to the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the direction or proportionality statement.

rubric.why: Checks the mathematical expression of the law.
rubric.description: Expresses Newton's second law as force equal to change in momentum divided by time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct force–momentum equation.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity: p = mv.
Newton’s second law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force.
The change in momentum takes place in the direction of the applied force.
For a change in momentum Δp during time Δt, F = Δp/Δt.

items.followUp: A stone is dropped from rest and reaches the ground in 4 s. Find the height fallen and its velocity on reaching the ground. Take g = 9.8 m/s².

rubric.why: Checks correct extraction of the given data and initial condition.
rubric.description: Identifies u = 0 m/s, t = 5 s, and g = 9.8 m/s².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the dropped-from-rest condition and the given values.

rubric.why: Checks the displacement equation and the calculated tower height.
rubric.description: Uses s = ut + ½gt² and obtains the height as 122.5 m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation/substitution and 1 mark for the correct height with unit.

rubric.why: Checks the velocity equation and the calculated impact velocity.
rubric.description: Uses v = u + gt and obtains 49 m/s downward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation/substitution and 1 mark for the correct velocity with direction.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 0 m/s, t = 5 s, g = 9.8 m/s².
Height: s = ut + ½gt².
Velocity on striking the ground: v = u + gt.
v = 0 m/s + (9.8 m/s²)(5 s) = 49 m/s downward.
